description: HTTP contract of every tingqr framework integration that serves a QR code as an SVG image (TypeScript: @tingqr/hono, @tingqr/nestjs; .NET: TingQR.AspNetCore). The app decides the payload (a resolve callback or a handler); no integration ever builds a QR from URL or query parameters.

success.when: the app gives a non-empty QR payload that renders
success.method: 200 for every HTTP method the app routes to it (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH…), never a framework default such as 201 for POST

empty.when: the app gives null, undefined/absent or an empty string
empty.body: not fixed (framework default); never an image

tingQrError.when: the app throws a TingQrError, or the payload or an option cannot be rendered
tingQrError.why: The app, not the client, builds the payload, so a TingQrError is a server-side mistake (e.g. a misconfigured receiving account). Its message may describe the app's configuration, so it is never sent to the client. An app that builds a QR from client input and wants 400 validates or encodes that input itself (e.g. inside resolve or the handler) and answers 400; errors from drawing the returned payload (too long for maxVersion, a logo too big for a small code) happen after it returns and are always 500.
tingQrError.log: The error (code and message) is written to the server log through the framework's usual channel: console.error for Hono (as Hono's default error handler does), Nest's Logger for NestJS.
tingQrError.note: Integrations whose framework routes errors through app filters (NestJS) guarantee the status and error.code only when the app does not rewrite the body.

otherErrors: left to the framework's normal error handling, unchanged

configuration.rule: every render option that does not depend on the payload (margin, colours, size, logo options, ecc, versions, mask, and the rule that a logo needs ecc H) is checked when the route or service is configured, with the same INVALID_VALUE errors and messages as toSvg; a mistake stops the app at startup, not every request
configuration.perRequest: only what depends on the payload: text too long for maxVersion, a logo too big for a small code (both 500 as tingQrError)
configuration.merged: where route options are merged over app-wide options at request time (NestJS @TingQrSvg over TingQrModule svg), a route foreground set without a route background is checked only as a colour at configuration time, because its contrast depends on the app-wide background; an app-wide/route clash is found per request
configuration.appWide: app-wide options (NestJS TingQrModule svg) are checked by rendering the receiving account's static code at startup, which also catches a logo too big for that code

logo.rule: a logo href must start with data:image/ (an SVG shown as an image cannot load a path or URL); anything else is INVALID_VALUE when the route or service is configured, not per request

notInContract: the status for a handler result that is not a string (a programming error)
